How does KV cache handle multi-tenant prefixes?
If we go Dedicated, can we pin instances by region?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan, Samira, Carlos, Priya, Liam, Nadia

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, um we'll do a quick run of items, check the gateway and creds, and then the SLO sanity check, Samira's gonna run through the recent bench results.
[00:18] Carlos: yep thanks Jordan, quick note, we had one test where responses were cut mid-token, not sure if it's streaming or tokenization.
[00:30] Samira: ok show of hands, that was probably the tokenizer mismatch we saw when using the open-source tokenizer, sometimes punctuation gets split differently, so there might be a small token delta that affects per-token billing and latency, we'll share the sample.
[00:52] Priya: we saw that too, also the KV cache hit rate seemed low on short prompts, do you think prefix caching is enabled in the staging run?
[01:05] Samira: yeah prefix caching was on but initial keys weren't normalized, so some misses. we pushed a small normalization patch, re-ran and hit rate improved 22 to 68 percent for the canonical set, uh caveat transcription: these numbers were from the short run not the 1k qps simulation.
[01:30] Liam: on the gateway side, we couldn't establish peering last week because of egress rules — I have a ticket open but wanted to confirm required ports and IPs.
[01:42] Jordan: noted, Liam, Samira can document the minimal CIDR and ports after this. but quick SSO question — Nadia any blockers on the SAML side?
[01:54] Nadia: only that we need a metadata XML and Redwood's SAML cert, and we prefer SP-initiated flows for auditability. also want to confirm KMS integration for envelope keys, are you supporting AWS KMS and HSM?
[02:12] Samira: we have native AWS KMS support and can do customer-managed CMKs; HSM-backed is on our roadmap but we do integrate via bring-your-own-key for Private deployments. we'll send notes.
[02:30] Jordan: ok next, SLO sanity, target for Orion was 95th p95 < 220ms for short prompts, and p99 < 400ms in staging do these still hold after the recent tuning?
[02:45] Priya: our observed p95 was 310ms on the baseline run, so above target, but after the KV normalization patch and small batching tweaks, p95 dropped to ~210ms in the short-run re-test. but the long-run 1k qps simulation shows p95 creeping back up to 260.
[03:10] Samira: yeah that matches our note: at steady 1k qps continuous batching fills except when sequence length variance spikes; we recommended dynamic batch cap of 12 for Orion's prompt distribution versus default 32, which keeps latency low but slightly increases compute ops.
[03:30] Carlos: tradeoffs — latency vs cost yes, can you quantify cost delta for changing batch cap from 32 to 12?
[03:40] Jordan: we'll put that in the spreadsheet — rough is +12% token compute cost but 30-40% p95 improvement for short prompts, exact depends on quantization.
[04:02] Priya: about quantization, we used 4-bit Q8 config on the test machines, any gotchas? model artifacts looked fine but logits divergence at tail tokens was visible, we want to avoid hallucination regressions.
[04:20] Samira: good point, quantization profiles are model-dependent, we have verified profiles for the model you're using (redwood-v2-open-ish), but we'll run additional A/B quality checks tied to your eval set. we'll upload the eval results.
[04:40] Liam: infrared (infr) sorry, infra question — if we move to Dedicated, can we pin machines to eu-west-1 only? compliance needs -- data residency.
[04:52] Jordan: yes Dedicated supports region pinning and private networking; for Private (on-prem/VPC) you can control all. we'll send the compliance pack and region SLA page.
[05:05] Nadia: audit logs, retention policy, and who can view tokens — we need RBAC examples, want to see how token-level logs are scrubbed.
[05:18] Samira: logs are configurable, by default we redact PII and user-provided keys, you can route logs to your SIEM via secure forwarder; we have an RBAC doc and can show role examples.
[05:40] Jordan: ok let's go briefly through the action items and timeline — Samira, did you get the dedicated bench scheduled?
[05:48] Samira: not yet, I need Priya's final prompt templates and a target qps, we suggested 100, 500, and 1000 sustained runs.
[06:00] Priya: we'll provide three prompt templates — a short, a medium and a long variant; short should be 8-24 tokens, medium 80-120, long 400+ for context.
[06:20] Carlos: also please include our fallback policy — if latency crosses 400ms for p99 we want automatic fallback to a smaller model, can Redwood do that?
[06:30] Samira: yes we have automatic fallback policies based on routing rules. you can set thresholds per route and fallback to a cheaper or lower-latency variant. we'll demo that in the next call.
[06:45] Liam: small note — during the run we saw occasional TLS renegotiation failures from one node, possible keepalive misconfig, we opened a cloud provider ticket.
[07:00] Jordan: ok we'll correlate logs, please upload the TLS stack traces to the shared sheet.
[07:12] Priya: quick question on key rotation, can we rotate API keys monthly without a blip to traffic? do you support dual-key rollover?
[07:22] Samira: yes dual-key rollover is supported, you can stage keys and rotate with zero-downtime assuming clients retry on 401 with a backoff. we'll provide a sample script.
[07:38] Carlos: last ops note — our billing team needs a per-token breakdown and an estimate for prefix caching impact, how granular can the billing be?
[07:48] Jordan: token-level breakdown per route is available in the console, and we can provide a CSV export for accounting. prefix cache savings will show as reduced tokens billed if you enable server-side prefix elision.
[08:05] Nadia: security snag — we want KMS to generate CMKs per-environment and have envelope keys never leave HSM, is BYOK supported right now?
[08:18] Samira: BYOK + AWS KMS CMKs is supported for Private deployments; for hosted we do CMK integration but not HSM export of keys. for on-prem we can discuss HSM connectors in detail.
[08:40] Jordan: great. wrapping up, recap: Jordan to send perf spreadsheet and SLO mapping, Samira to share SAML metadata and KMS notes, Priya to send prompts, Liam to confirm VPC peering details. Dedicated bench scheduling tentatively week of 2026-11-09.
[09:05] Carlos: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[09:12] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up in email, talk soon.

Notes & imperfections: transcription occasionally swapped names (e.g., Liam recorded as "Len" in the raw), some timestamps approximate. References: shared drive link - "Orion-Redwood-POC/benchmarks" (internal), security pack link - "redwood.com/security/orion-pack.pdf" (placeholder).
